projects.hexacalm.title: Hexacalm｜3D Hex World and Dynamic Soundscapes
projects.hexacalm.coverAlt: Promotional illustration of the Hexacalm floating hex world, not an application screenshot
projects.hexacalm.summary: An editable 3D world with dynamic audio mixing, combining hex coordinates, connected roads, and character movement into a relaxing experience.
projects.hexacalm.cardTitle.subtitle: 3D Interaction & Soundscapes
projects.hexacalm.meta.role.label: Role
projects.hexacalm.meta.technology.label: Stack
projects.hexacalm.meta.assets.label: Assets
projects.hexacalm.introduction: Hexacalm is my 3D hex world and soundscape application. Users can place forests, water, roads, and buildings, add pets that walk along the roads, and switch to relaxation mode to watch the world. It combines spatial interaction, world state, and audio control in one browser experience. The image above is a promotional illustration; the images below are asset previews.
projects.hexacalm.technology: Built with React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Zustand, Tone.js, Tailwind CSS, and Vite. Hex coordinates, road connections, character movement, and audio mixing are separated into pure logic modules, keeping rendering and state transitions clearly defined.
projects.hexacalm.contribution: Implemented hex world building, road connections, character movement, history and persistence, and the integration of 3D scenes with audio. The project explores how geometry algorithms and browser interactions can become a usable product. Models and asset previews use Kenney assets (CC0).
projects.hexacalm.features.placement.des: Axial coordinates unify tile indexing and conversion to 3D positions. When placing roads or rivers, the system checks neighboring exits and compares six rotations to choose the orientation with the most connections.
projects.hexacalm.features.placement.alt: Preview of a Kenney hex road intersection asset
projects.hexacalm.features.history.title: Reversible building state
projects.hexacalm.features.history.descr: Zustand centralizes placement, replacement, rotation, and removal. History snapshots support up to 50 undo and redo steps. World and audio settings are saved to localStorage, with structure and version checks on loading.
projects.hexacalm.features.soundscapes.t: Soundscapes that respond to the world
projects.hexacalm.features.soundscapes.d: Audio mixing is calculated from tile composition and distance weights around characters. Sound priorities and replacement thresholds control ambient audio, while Tone.js volume transitions and fades make changes feel less abrupt.
projects.hexacalm.features.movement.desc: Roads connect through matching exits in both directions. Distance interpolation and look-ahead direction calculations handle turns, junctions, and dead ends, with world, third-person, and first-person views.
projects.hexacalm.features.movement.alt: Preview of a Kenney cat character asset
projects.hexacalm.features.rendering.des: GLTFLoader loads models with shared textures and cloned scenes. On-demand rendering, animation updates, and a device pixel ratio cap control rendering cost. The application also handles unavailable WebGL and lost rendering contexts.
projects.agentService.title: AI Conversation Service Integration
projects.agentService.summary: Integrated GCP CES with multimodal conversations, sessions, and contextual data.
projects.agentService.introduction: Contributed to an enterprise AI conversation service integration centered on GCP CES, bringing cloud conversation capabilities, text, images, and context into the application. This overview focuses on the integration between cloud AI services and product interfaces.
projects.agentService.technology: Used the GCP CES SDK to connect cloud conversation sessions, with Node.js and Fastify providing an integration layer for multimodal data conversion, conversation responses, and rate limiting.
projects.agentService.contribution: Implemented multimodal input, context transmission, and response handling for the GCP CES integration, along with rate limiting, cache control, and deployment version identifiers. Scope reflects my own commits.
projects.agentService.features.integrati: Connected conversation sessions through the cloud SDK and transformed service responses into formats usable by the interface, linking AI capabilities with product interactions.
projects.agentService.features.multimoda: Integrated text, images, and structured context, converting data between the application and cloud service to support ongoing conversations.
projects.agentService.features.traffic.d: Combined burst and sustained rate limits to reject excess requests early, and configured response caching according to the characteristics of conversation data.
projects.agentService.features.deploymen: Added deployment version identifiers to confirm environments and trace integration issues.
projects.visualWorkflow.title: Visual AI Workflow
projects.visualWorkflow.summary: Used AI-assisted development to deliver an interactive workflow prototype/MVP within one month.
projects.visualWorkflow.meta.scope.label: Scope
projects.visualWorkflow.introduction: Contributed to a visual AI workflow tool with a prototype/MVP scope. Multi-step AI operations became editable, executable node graphs, enabling hands-on use and rapid feedback.
projects.visualWorkflow.technology: Combined Next.js, React Flow, Zustand, and IndexedDB for editing, execution, and persistence, with AI-assisted development shortening implementation cycles. The focus was on keeping the MVP scope manageable while maintaining module boundaries between graphs, state, and storage.
projects.visualWorkflow.contribution: Used AI-assisted development to deliver the prototype/MVP. Contributed to the editor and feature nodes, implementing graph layout, data layers, media retrieval, execution coordination, and improvements to result inspection.
projects.visualWorkflow.features.deliver: Focused on an interactive prototype/MVP and used AI-assisted development to deliver core node editing, workflow execution, and result inspection.
Arranged nodes in layers based on dependencies, accounting for node dimensions and spacing to improve the readability of complex workflows.
projects.visualWorkflow.features.persist: Separated interaction state, document data, and storage interfaces. Hooks coordinate saving and reduce coupling between the UI and IndexedDB.
projects.visualWorkflow.features.media.d: Identified media by content hashes so documents and execution records could store references, with centralized media resolution and retrieval for the interface.
projects.visualWorkflow.features.executi: Scheduled execution according to dependencies, handling concurrency limits, cancellation, and result states. Feature definitions, configuration interfaces, and execution logic are separated and connected through registration and lazy loading.
projects.apiWorkspace.title: Multi-Application Service Platform
projects.apiWorkspace.summary: Collaborated across teams on a large, long-running Nx project, maintaining multiple applications and shared libraries.
projects.apiWorkspace.meta.scope.label: Scope
projects.apiWorkspace.introduction: Contributed to a large, long-running project managed with Nx, collaborating across teams on multiple applications and shared libraries. This overview focuses on shared code consistency, the impact of changes across libraries, and ongoing maintenance.
projects.apiWorkspace.technology: Used Nx to manage React/Next.js applications and shared libraries, with TanStack Query, Zustand, and i18next supporting data interactions and internationalization. The focus was on keeping shared libraries consistent through cross-team collaboration and long-term development.
projects.apiWorkspace.contribution: Contributed to shared calculations, asynchronous interactions, responsive content, and resource loading in a long-running, multi-team project. Scope reflects my own commits; the overall Nx architecture is a team achievement.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.collabora: Developed features across applications and shared libraries while considering team coordination, shared library usage, and the impact of changes on different applications.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.calculati: Consolidated calculation rules into shared modules to reduce duplicated implementations and inconsistent results across pages.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.asyncStat: Centralized form data and clarified responsibilities for polling and interaction state, reducing duplicate state and unnecessary UI updates.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.responsiv: Handled images and videos across device conditions and maintained consistency between static output and client-side hydration.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.loading.d: Improved syntax highlighting by loading languages and themes on demand and sharing initialization results.
projects.apiWorkspace.features.localized: Developed multi-step calculation interfaces, organizing parameter selection, input controls, and result presentation, and improving localized error messages.
projects.onlineExam.title: Online Examination System
projects.onlineExam.summary: Built a full-stack system for daily practice, mock exams, and score rankings, from requirements interviews through development and deployment.
projects.onlineExam.meta.role.label: Role
projects.onlineExam.introduction: This project moved examination practice from an in-person-only setting to the web, giving users a more convenient way to take practice tests.
projects.onlineExam.technology.details: (MongoDB, Express.js, React, and Node.js) to simplify development through an end-to-end JavaScript solution. MongoDB provides flexible storage, Express.js and Node.js power the backend, and React enables dynamic, responsive interfaces.
projects.onlineExam.contribution: Responsible for planning, user interviews, interface design, development, and deployment.
projects.onlineExam.features.dailyPracti: Scheduled tests by date so students could build a habit of practicing every day.
projects.onlineExam.features.mockExam.de: Modeled the interface on Taiwan's Ministry of Examination test screens so students could practice in an environment similar to the actual exam.
projects.onlineExam.features.rankings.de: Compared student scores through rankings, using friendly competition to encourage participation and motivation.
projects.chatbotConfig.title: Chatbot Configuration Editor
projects.chatbotConfig.summary: Combined configuration management and caching to support chatbot configuration updates.
projects.chatbotConfig.meta.role.label: Role
projects.chatbotConfig.introduction: An internal configuration editor that lets organizations customize and manage chatbot settings, including greetings, phone numbers, and addresses. It addresses frequent configuration changes by enabling updates without code changes, improving flexibility and maintainability.
projects.chatbotConfig.technology: Built with React on the frontend and Fastify on the backend. Data is stored in Google Firestore with Redis caching, and the system is deployed on Google Cloud Platform.
projects.chatbotConfig.contribution: Led frontend/backend integration and was responsible for system architecture, caching, and database setup. Interviewed internal users to refine features, and tailored caching behavior to the main chatbot service.
projects.chatbotConfig.features.configur: Users can create, edit, delete, and group configuration entries. The system synchronizes updates across multiple servers to keep configurations current.
Redis caches configuration reads so the chatbot can avoid querying Firestore on every request, particularly under frequent reads. Firestore provides persistent storage, balancing performance and reliability.
